title.narrative: Ukuthula Trust: Navigating a Path to Reviving Democracy in Zimbabwe 2021 - 2024
Ukuthula Trust: Navigating a Path to Reviving Democracy in Zimbabwe 2021 - 2024

description.narrative:
The Ukuthula Trust seeks to achieve these broader objectives through the following objectives:
Project Goal: To deepen democracy by empowering people to release their energy towards taking an active part in the development and governance of their communities, through rehabilitation of communities and through prevention of conflict in Zimbabwe in the future by generating knowledge and promoting accountability.
1. Deepening Democracy: To empower and promote poor and marginalized communities, especially women and youth, in a bid to increase local and national government transparency, accountability and responsiveness to those communities 2. Restoring Social Fabric and Rehabilitating Victims of Collective Violence: To improve community cohesion, including women and youth, so that all community members can actively participate in the development of their community. 3. Generating Knowledge: To actively promote the re-examining of concepts linked to democracy, youth, gender, development and the histories of violence in Zimbabwe. 4. Lobbying and Advocacy: To promote and influence policy change in Zimbabwe.

The Ukuthula Trust seeks to achieve these broader objectives through the following objectives:
Project Goal: To deepen democracy by empowering people to release their energy towards taking an active part in the development and governance of their communities, through rehabilitation of communities and through prevention of conflict in Zimbabwe in the future by generating knowledge and promoting accountability.
1. Deepening Democracy: To empower and promote poor and marginalized communities, especially women and youth, in a bid to increase local and national government transparency, accountability and responsiveness to those communities
2. Restoring Social Fabric and Rehabilitating Victims of Collective Violence: To improve community cohesion, including women and youth, so that all community members can actively participate in the development of their community.
3. Generating Knowledge: To actively promote the re-examining of concepts linked to democracy, youth, gender, development and the histories of violence in Zimbabwe.
4. Lobbying and Advocacy: To promote and influence policy change in Zimbabwe.

Ukuthula Trust försöker uppnå dessa bredare mål genom följande:
Projektmål: Att fördjupa demokratin genom att ge människor möjlighet att aktivt ta del i utvecklingen och styrningen av sina samhällen, genom rehabilitering av samhällen, och genom att förebygga framtida konflikter i Zimbabwe genom att generera kunskap och främja ansvarsskyldighet. 1.Fördjupad demokrati: Att stärka och främja fattiga och marginaliserade samhällen, med särskilt fokus på kvinnor och ungdomar, i ett försök att öka den lokala och nationella regeringens öppenhet, ansvarsskyldighet och lyhördhet för dessa samhällen.
2.Återställa social struktur och rehabilitera offer för kollektivt våld: Att förbättra samhällets sammanhållning, inklusive kvinnor och ungdomar, så att alla medlemmar i samhället aktivt kan delta i utvecklingen.
3.Skapa kunskap: Att aktivt främja omprövning av begrepp kopplade till demokrati, ungdom, kön, utveckling och historiskt våld i Zimbabwe.
4.Lobbying och påverkansarbete: Att främja och påverka politiska förändringar i Zimbabwe.

The following are the results achieved by the programme during the period January 2023 to February 2024. During the period under review the programme carried out most of its the work in Lupane and Tsholotsho in Matabeleland North and in Gwanda in Matabeleland South, targeting community members, traditional leaders, church leaders and the community. The programme actively targeted women and youth in its activities, who continue to be a marginalized group, with the aim of promoting their inclusion and active participation in community development initiatives and decision-making processes.
The pogramme also worked with local authorities in the target districts as well as with the different development committees that include the Ward and Village Development Committees (WADCOS & VIDCOS) and school development committees as well as with local professionals that include health care workers and law enforcement officers. Access to the different communities was through individual and group meetings as well as workshops and church services.
The collaboration of Ukuthula with Blanket Mine at Enqameni Reflection Centre has seen the centre grow. The centre now has running water, a perimeter fence and poles and cables for solar power have been erected and the centre should be electrified very soon. Following this, plans are underway, also with assistance from Blanket Mine, to connect the centre to the internet, as a means of widening the worldview of beneficiaries.
New classes were introduced at Enyandeni and Enqameni centres following lobbying by the youth. At Enyandeni, hairdressing was introduced, while at Enqameni, sewing and brick laying were introduced, resulting in a significant increase in enrolment at both centres.
In November, 66 students graduated at Enqameni in computers, sewing and brick-laying while at Enyandeni 72 students graduated in computers, welding, building, sewing, hairdressing and food-preparation. The Enyandeni garden and poultry projects continued to thrive, with beans, carrots, tomatoes, beetroot and chomolia being grown throughout the year, with beneficiaries making a decent profit. This also benefitted the local community as it afforded them access to cheaper nutritious vegetables throughout the year.
As a result of these projects, the women and youth report improved livelihoods as they are now socio-economically empowered. Some of the married women report improved relations in their homes as a result of their financial contributions. The programme has contributed to reduced economically based gender based violence.
Following extensive engagement with traditional and church leaders as well as the community, more women and youth are now actively involved in key leadership positions that include membership in the VIDCO, WADCO and School Development Committees.
There was significant depoliticization of a number of traditional leaders in Lupane resulting in enhanced community cohesion and improved development. This was a significant outcome as many traditional leaders have in the past always aligned themselves to political parties to the detriment of development in their communities. Political affiliation was a major driver of polarization as people supported development initiatives proposed or led by like-minded leaders. This move has seen communities coming together and making collective decisions that benefit the entire community. Conflict transformation was a major achievement in Lupane and Gwanda. Ukuthula worked with traditional and other community leaders in this regard. One of the major outcomes was the adoption by traditional leaders of a reparative approach to conflict management as opposed to the punitive approach they were using. By using this approach they testify that people are able to move forward with dignity and relations are repaired.
The Ukuthula Trust Forensic Anthropology Team (UFAT) worked closely with chiefs in Matabeleland around Gukurahundi exhumations. Five graves, including mass graves, were exhumed in Matabeleland North and South. This contributed to the beginning of the healing process for not just the affected families but also their communities as well. A healed community is able to be forward looking and work together towards development. 72 chiefs and 1 396 members of the chiefs panel -these include people to offer psychosocial support, rapporteurs for documentation and pastors- being trained. This has strengthened their capacity to lead the anticipated Gukurahundi village-by-village hearings.
